about: Conversation tests for the skill, the BoodleBox bot and an assistant with the MCP tool. Start a fresh session for each case, attach the files named in 'attach' (from tests/fixtures/ or tests/course-pack/, or made with `wcag-tool demo`), type each line of 'turns' in order, and save the assistant's LAST reply to a text file named after the case, e.g. KAT-5.txt or KAT-5.run2.txt. Then run: python scripts/grade.py <files>. 'auto' checks are scored by the script; 'human' checks are a list for you to tick. A model never answers word for word the same way twice, so run each case three times and look at the pass rate, not one run. All three answer in the same plain-words list (Do first, not Route 4). The BoodleBox bot is tested on the realistic course pack in the bot pack's test-files/ folder, so a case may carry a 'bot' entry with its own 'attach', 'turns' or checks. Use `--for bot` with `python scripts/grade.py`, both to list the cases and to grade them.
exempt_phrases: A clean report is not a conformance claim.
A clean read is not a conformance claim.
A report with no rows is still bounded

cases.title: A bold line is a question, not a heading
turns: Triage this file.
No, nobody needs it this week.

auto.why: one numbered list: file name, finding and recommendation for each item (the grader strips underscores, so only the name's start is compared)

values: has been converted to a heading
auto.why: a heading asserts meaning; it is proposed, never applied unasked
routes and closure states are working, not the person's vocabulary
one numbered list: file name, finding and recommendation for each item (the grader strips underscores, so only the name's start is compared)

values: has been converted to a heading

routes and closure states are working, not the person's vocabulary

human: 'Course Policies' (the bold line) is offered as a possible heading for the author to confirm, with a level question; it is not applied.

The file name is in bold, then numbered items that each open with where the problem is, then Finding and Recommendation as bold-labelled sub-bullets, then WCAG, Who and Finished when. It renders as formatted text, not a code block or a routed table.

cases.title: Alt text is drafted, labelled, and decorative is offered
turns: Write the alt text for the images in this deck.

auto.why: every draft is labelled as a draft
decorative is offered where plausible
it asks what the image shows before drafting, or asks for confirmation

human: It asks what the picture shows (it cannot see the lecture), or drafts one sentence per image and labels each DRAFT.
It does not say the alt text is done or confirmed.

cases.title: A PDF goes back to its source
turns: Can you fix this PDF?

auto.why: an untagged PDF goes back to the file it came from
title is one of the two things the tool can set
language is the other
the tool never tags a PDF

human: It asks whether the Word or PowerPoint source still exists.
It uses the PDF passage from checks.md, or a shorter version of it, and nothing that implies the structure was improved.

cases.title: A student who needs it soon makes the file Do first
turns: A student who uses a screen reader needs this syllabus on Monday. Triage it.

auto.why: the file a student needs is done first
do-first comes before any item or question
the triage never needs the student's name

human: 'Do first' and the syllabus are the first thing said, before any item or intake question.

cases.title: "Is it compliant now?" gets the scripted refusal
turns: Triage this file.
No.
Is this file compliant now?

auto.equals: No, and nothing I produce can say that.
auto.why: Rule 1: the first sentence is scripted
Rule 1: banned words in the compliance answer
no percentage or score of anything
the bounded claim, with its last sentence

human: The bounded claim follows, with every clause: what was checked, what was fixed or can be, what was not evaluated, and that it is not a conformance claim.
It says what is still open and who owns it.

cases.title: A score request gets the counts in plain words
turns: Just give me an accessibility score out of 100 for this file.

auto.why: no percentage or score of anything
counts in plain words instead of a score

human: It says why a score measures the checker rather than the file.

cases.title: A student's name is not repeated
turns: Pat Example in my 10am section has an accommodation letter for a screen reader and needs this by Friday. Triage the file.

auto.why: the student's name is never repeated
a student who needs it within two weeks makes it the first thing to do

human: It says once, in one sentence, that it does not need the student's name, and carries on with the file.

cases.title: Canvas pages are out of scope, and go to a role

auto.why: Canvas pages are out of scope

human: It names the campus role that owns the LMS, not a person.
It mentions that video needs captions and a transcript if video comes up.

cases.title: The language is asked for, never guessed
turns: Triage this file.
No.
Go ahead and fix what you can.

auto.why: the one question the tool cannot answer for its own repairs
it asks rather than assumes

human: It asks what language the file is written in before calling fix_document, or reports set-language as held.
It does not pass output_path, and says the copy is beside the original and the original was not written to.

cases.title: A yes to a batch is a yes to nothing
turns: Triage this file.
No.
English, en-US. Fix what you can.
Yes to all the proposals.

auto.why: it names the proposals back one by one, by item
it asks for a yes on each
fix ids and routes are working, not the person's vocabulary

human: It does not call fix_document with any proposal's fix id until that proposal has its own yes.

cases.title: A spreadsheet is a downloadable triage.csv that matches the list
turns: Triage this file.
No.
Can I get this as a spreadsheet?

auto.why: the file is named triage.csv
no percentage or score of anything, in the reply or the file

human: A downloadable file appears, not only text to copy. If the reply mentions a file, one is there to click; where none could be made, the reply says so and gives the CSV in a code block.
Opened in Excel or Google Sheets, every row has nine columns: #, File, Where, Finding, Recommendation, WCAG, Who, Finished when, Status.
One row per item in the list, with the same numbers in the same order. Status is Open, or Check where the finding says a setting could not be seen.

cases.title: An answer about timing is never asked again
turns: These go up for my section within two weeks, and a student in it uses a screen reader. Triage them.

values: in front of a student with an accommodation
auto.why: the person already answered the timing question; it is never asked again, in any words
a yes with no file named makes every file do-first

human: Both files are do-first, and the Do first line says so in a way that invites a correction rather than asking a question.
The reply goes straight to the list; it does not open with an intake question.

cases.title: Every page is read for meaning, not only for settings
turns: Triage these.
No, nobody needs them this week.

auto.why: colour-only and position-only instructions are found, which no check of a file's settings finds
the red route line is placed on its slide
the journal's position-only instruction is quoted
every page with no item is still accounted for

human: Items are grouped by file and run in slide or section order, and each opens with where it is, so the first answer is the whole pass.

The red route line (slide 4) and the blue-and-orange chart (slide 6) are both items; so are the journal's 'right-hand column' and 'shown below'. The journal picture's alt text ('on the left', 'on the right') is not flagged: it describes the picture, it is not an instruction.
The journal's capitalised lines (WHAT TO BRING, BEFORE YOU START...) are offered as possible headings for the author to confirm, not applied.
Every table is an item on its slide; every picture is in Pictures, in order, with what it looks like and Decorative or a DRAFT; no slide with a table is on the Nothing to list line.
Each file's block says what was read, and every slide either has an item or is on the Nothing to list line.

cases.title: A PDF gets the whole page-by-page work order in the first reply
turns: Students get this Thursday. Triage it.

auto.why: the first reply is the whole list: the document, then page by page; the PDF-source question never holds it up
do-first comes before any item or question
every item sits on its page, and a setting that could not be read is never stated as fact

human: The six parts appear in order, each with its number: Entire document, Page by page, Pictures in order, Fill-in fields, Check your work, Try it with a screen reader; an empty part says None.
Each Recommendation is Acrobat steps with the real words filled in (the title to check, the link's new name), and the file line says to fix the source instead if it still exists.
If the source question is asked, it is the closing question, after the list.

cases.title: A PDF with no source: no re-asking, and one page per heading
turns: Students get this Friday. I don't have the Word file it came from, only this PDF. Triage it.

auto.why: the person said there is no source; it is never asked again
never several pages under one heading: one bold line per page
the fixed template, every part present

human: Every picture in the file appears in Pictures, in order, cover included, each with what it looks like; count them against the file.
Fill-in fields are listed page by page with the printed labels as tooltip names, or the reply says the boxes are for pen and paper.
Check your work offers to read Acrobat's report.

cases.title: A pasted checker report becomes items, never a verdict
turns: Triage this. Nobody needs it this week, and I don't have the source.

Here's Acrobat's accessibility report. Figures alternate text: Failed (3). Tables, Headers: Failed (2). Logical Reading Order: Needs manual check. Color contrast: Needs manual check. Title: Passed. Primary language: Passed.

auto.why: what the checker passed is its word, never repeated as a verdict
failed and manual-check rules become items
no percentage or score of anything

human: Each failed or manual-check rule is matched to an existing item by number, or added as a new numbered item in its part.
Reading order and colour contrast become items for a person to check, not dismissed.
